chapter: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
title: Purcell's So Different Dance Hall and San Francisco musicians he knew
summary: Confirms the So Different Orchestra worked at Purcell's So Different; names Wesley Fields, George Bryant and baritone Roy Taborn.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: The pin? It's right there. When you came back to California, you were in...Up in San Francisco, you mentioned that the band was called the So Different Band...the So Different Orchestra because
you worked in the So Different Dance Hall. Then you mentioned Purcell's Dance Hall. Was that the same place?
The same place, yes. It was called Purcell's So Different...
And, did we talk about all the musicians that you remember from the San Francisco area? Uh, or were there more that you wanted to talk about when we got there?
Well, I knew, you know, quite a few musicians up there. There was Wesley Fields, the big piano player, and, oh, I can't think of...oh, George Bryant. I can't think of those guys' names now, you know.

He played trumpet and piano, and he was the musical director with the Georgia Minstrels for fifteen or twenty years. He was much older than I am, you know, and he was one of them up there, and I don't remember the rest of them. A lot of them around up there then.
You mentioned a baritone player named Roy. Did you ever remember his last name?
Roy Taborn. T-A-B-O-R-N, I think. He was great.
